_about: Key votes on member pages. Hand-picked, in the order of the issues voters rated most important to their vote (Pew Research Center, October 8, 2026): one vote per issue, a second only for a major law. head = what a Yes vote supported. law = signing date if it became law, else omitted (the page then shows the House result only). Only bills with a House vote get a row; a competing bill on the same goal is noted in one neutral line (competing). Outcomes checked against congress.gov; see python/scratch/key_votes/ for sources.

119.head: Extend tax cuts, cut Medicaid and food aid
119.what: Extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds tax breaks on tips, overtime and for seniors, cuts projected Medicaid and food-aid (SNAP) spending, adds money for border enforcement and defense, and raises the debt limit.

119.head: Require proof of citizenship to register to vote
119.what: Requires documents proving U.S. citizenship, such as a passport or birth certificate, to register to vote in federal elections.

119.head: Bar Congress from buying stocks, require photo ID to vote
119.what: Bars members of Congress, their spouses and dependent children from buying individual stocks. They may keep stocks they already own but must give 7 days' public notice before selling. Also requires photo ID to vote in person.
119.competing: A competing Democratic bill (H.R. 6731) would also cover the President and Vice President and require selling stocks already owned. It never got a House vote.

119.head: Expand small-business health plans, lower some premiums
119.official: Lower Health Care Premiums for All Americans Act (H.R. 6703)
119.what: Lets small businesses band together to buy health plans, expands employer accounts for buying individual coverage, funds payments that lower some marketplace premiums from 2027, and adds reporting rules for drug-benefit middlemen. Does not extend the larger ACA subsidies.
119.competing: The House also voted on a competing bill to extend the larger ACA subsidies (next on this list).

119.head: Extend ACA premium subsidies for 3 years
119.what: Extends the larger Affordable Care Act premium subsidies, which ended with 2025, through 2028.
119.competing: The House also voted on a competing Republican health bill (previous on this list).

119.head: Add $70 billion for ICE and Border Patrol
119.what: Adds about $70 billion for immigration enforcement and border security through 2029, passed by a simple majority under budget rules.

119.head: Lend Ukraine $8 billion for weapons, add Russia sanctions
119.what: Provides $8 billion in loans for Ukraine to buy weapons, extends U.S. military aid to Ukraine through 2027, and adds sanctions on Russia.

119.head: Permanently ban fentanyl look-alike drugs
119.what: Permanently lists fentanyl-related drugs with the most dangerous controlled substances, with mandatory minimum sentences for trafficking them.

119.head: Require care for infants who survive an abortion
119.what: Requires doctors to give an infant born alive during an attempted abortion the same care as any newborn, with criminal penalties.

119.head: Stop the VA from flagging some veterans in gun checks
119.what: Stops the VA from reporting veterans who have someone managing their benefits to the gun background-check system unless a judge finds them dangerous.

119.head: End the 2025 government shutdown
119.what: Ends the 43-day shutdown, funds the government through January 30, 2026, and passes full-year funding for food aid, veterans and military construction.

118.head: Expand the child tax credit
118.official: Tax Relief for American Families and Workers Act (H.R. 7024)
118.what: Expands the child tax credit for lower-income families and restores several business tax breaks.

118.head: End Social Security cuts for public-sector retirees
118.what: Ends two rules that cut Social Security benefits for many teachers, police officers and other public workers with pensions.

118.head: Require proof of citizenship to register to vote
118.what: Requires documents proving U.S. citizenship, such as a passport or birth certificate, to register to vote in federal elections.

118.head: Require hospitals and insurers to post prices
118.what: Requires hospitals, insurers and drug-benefit middlemen to publish prices, and changes some Medicare drug payments.

118.head: Cancel Biden's student loan forgiveness
118.what: Overturns President Biden's plan to forgive up to $20,000 in federal student loans per borrower.

118.head: Tighten asylum rules, restart the border wall
118.what: Restarts border wall construction, tightens asylum rules and requires employers to check workers' immigration status (E-Verify).

118.head: Send $61 billion in aid to Ukraine
118.law: April 24, 2024, in a combined foreign aid package
118.what: Provides about $61 billion in military and economic aid to Ukraine.

118.head: Send $26 billion in aid to Israel and for Gaza relief
118.law: April 24, 2024, in a combined foreign aid package
118.what: Provides about $26 billion for Israel's defense and for humanitarian aid, including in Gaza.

118.head: Expand oil, gas and mining, speed energy permits
118.what: Expands oil, gas and mining on federal land and water and speeds up permits for energy projects.

118.head: Require care for infants who survive an abortion
118.what: Requires doctors to give an infant born alive during an attempted abortion the same care as any newborn, with criminal penalties.

118.head: Overturn the ATF pistol-brace rule
118.what: Cancels a federal rule that treated pistols fitted with stabilizing braces like short-barreled rifles, which must be registered.

118.head: Suspend the debt limit and cap spending
118.what: Suspends the debt limit until 2025 to avoid a default and caps federal spending for two years.
